content: Cattle die, kinsmen die, and you yourself must die; but the fair fame of an honorable life never dies.
author: Celtic & Norse Proverbs
sourceWork: Deyr fé, deyja frændr (Hávamál, Stanza 76) — The Poetic Edda
explanation: In the severe Nordic climate, our ancestors recognized the unsparing truth: wealth vanishes in famine, companions fall in battle, and our own breath will soon cease. The only treasure immune to time and decay is the unblemished reputation of having walked with honor and courage.
practicalInsight: Make your moral choices today with an eye toward how you wish to be spoken of after you are gone.
reflectionPrompt: When your possessions have vanished, what kind of honor and deeds will remain attached to your name?
